messages.author: d3da5cb25684a162
messages.subject: Surveys which combine both point and line transects
parts:
I am currently working on a dataset of opportunistic distance sightings from
a marine mammal monitoring program. My aim is to create a Generalized
Additive Model which will allow me to predict density and distribution of
cetaceans within my study area. Because the vessel both travels through the
study area and spends time monitoring vessel activity around killer whales
there are times when the vessel is traveling at different speeds. I can
determine when the vessel was monitoring and when they were transiting. As
such, I wondered if it made sense to analyze the sightings collected when
monitoring (travelling at less than 5 knots) as point transects in Distance
and when the vessel is transiting to analyze them as line transects. The
difficulty with this is that I am not sure how this will affect how I build
the model as I will have different detection functions depending on what the
vessel is doing?

I was also wondering if one way to tackle this issue would be to use vessel
speed as a covariate in the MCDS function of Distance - or if that is at all
appropriate.

Any thoughts on this would be much appreciated.

Thank You
Nicole

--

Nicole Koshure
Master's Candidate
Fisheries Research Group
School of Resource and Environmental Management
Simon Fraser University, Burnaby, BC
nm...@sfu.ca

messages.author: 5140016d70f6ba82
messages.subject: Re: Surveys which combine both point and line transects
parts:
Nicole-

Transit speed can affect detection probability and you can use it as a
covariate for it. I have a recent ms on this in regard to aircraft
speed in Wildlife Research. However, with marine mammals you have the
added complication that vessel speed also affects the probability that
the critter is available at the surface. This aspect will not be
handled using vessel speed as a covariate because it will affect g(0)
which is not incorporated into DISTANCE.

I would not recommend treating your data as a point transect unless what
you have is cue counting data.

regards --jeff
